The blocker is a genuine tooling limitation, which I verified: the dossier has no own_terms record, jobs/claim-kit/assemble.py event() takes actor from the end record's actor_id/instrument_id and mechanism from the CSV row's 'mechanism' or the record's mechanism/verb/kind, and batch.py CLAUSE_FIELDS has no mechanism column; CLAUSES:EO:5763#whole has no actor and kind 'whole', ORIGINAL:EO:5763 has no mechanism. Read jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5881.txt in full. Inventory: one operative sentence (further exemption of William L. Hill, John Lewis May, Leonard Magruder 'and continued in the service until August 1, 1932') plus a purpose statement that is not an independent command; one-clause inventory is complete. End date 1932-08-01 is the order's own stated term; the 'July 10, 1932' in the same sentence is the recited term of EO 5874 (June 30, 1932), which I confirmed in jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5874.txt (lines 3233-3238 list Magruder, Hill, John L. May under Treasury; term 'until July 10, 1932'). The producer correctly overrode the machine TERM record, whose stated_end_date/effective_date 1932-07-10 is wrong; the claim's first_end date (1932-08-01) is right and its quoted span contains 'until August 1, 1932'. Caveat for the human reviewer: the cited TERM evidence record still carries the wrong machine date. The purpose sentence ('for such period only as is absolutely necessary to afford time in which to appoint successors') states the reason for the fixed term; it is not a condition that ends the grant earlier on a successor's appointment. Producer's statement that EO 5874 is outside the identity universe is accurate (jobs/ofr-compilations/output/CENSUS_LEADS.csv marks EO:5874 NOT_IN_CENSUS). No later order naming any of the three persons in WPA, Hoover texts (only EO 5874 and EO 5881 contain the names) or APP index. Savings: accrued service/pay only; acceptable. Search re-run by reviewer: whitespace-insensitive surname/full-name search of every entry of jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv (numbered EOs through the WPA 1944 list, so covering the 1932-1937 gap before the OFR catalog), grep of all 526 held Hoover OFR 1974 texts (EO 5550-6070) and of the APP title index (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/INDEX.csv, which also lists FDR 1933 orders). Context found: EO 6142 (May 23, 1933) shows that early termination of a section-204 exemption by a later order did occur in this family (Pickens Neagle, EO 5872), so the earlier-end question is real; no such order names this order's person(s). EO 6142 and EO 6146 (May 23/26, 1933) also show section 204 still being administered through May 31, 1933, which is stronger corroboration of the statute's continuity than the producer's 1934-35 examples. Residual, not a defect: unnumbered orders and orders whose WPA summary omits names are not fully excluded. Observation for a correction version: the claim's structured later_source_search lists only the USC, eCFR and OFR catalog (1937 onward) searches; the decisive pre-1937 WPA/Hoover-text search is recorded only in research_rationale prose and should be added as its own later_source_search entry. original_pages_confirmed is false: the page images were not checked (the OFR 1974 PDF is an LFS pointer in this checkout), so the date rests on the OCR layer, which reads cleanly.
